title: Answer: systems with temporally deep generative models are conscious, and a virus is not

statements.text: Anything that revisits its characteristic states can be read as inferring, but only a system whose generative model has temporal depth is conscious. A virus has the self-organizing, implicitly inferential dynamics of a living thing, yet it is not conscious, even when it responds adaptively. A creature with a deep, temporally thick model is self-evidencing in a prospective and purposeful way. The same person loses consciousness, as in dreamless sleep, whenever that model loses its thickness and becomes as thin as a virus's.
statements.scope: Am I self-conscious? (2018), section Viruses and vegans

sources.quote: a virus possesses all the biotic, self-organizing and implicitly inferential dynamics to qualify as a process of Bayesian inference
Put simply, this suggests that viruses are not conscious; even if they respond adaptively from the point of view of a selective process.
Vegans, on the other hand, with deep (temporally thick) generative models are self-evidencing in a prospective and purposeful way
loss of consciousness occurs whenever our generative models lose their "thickness" and become as "thin" as a viruses.
